My new favorite vibe coding stack:

OpenCode + the "Oh My OpenCode" plugin. 

It is a multi-agent setup that utilizes Opus 4.5 as an orchestrator that delegates tasks to other models best suited for the job:

· Opus 4.5 - main driver + delegator
· GPT 5.2 - architecture & code review
· Sonnet 4.5 - context-efficient docs lookup
· Grok Code - fast codebase exploration
· Gemini 3 Pro -  frontend UI/UX work
· Gemini 3 Flash - writing docs & file analysis

Spent my Sunday building an app with this, and it was super impressive - will be sharing more soon!

tweets.text:
I see this problem all the time with non-technical founders who are just getting into vibe coding.

At the start, everything feels amazing. AI builds the frontend fast, things look polished, and it feels like the app is basically done. BIG dopamine hit.

Then you start adding the backend. Things get a little harder. A few bugs show up.

But the real pain hits in the last 5%.

That’s where things start breaking. You realize parts of the app were never wired properly, edge cases were ignored, and fixing it now feels harder than starting over. This is where most people give up, or end up hiring an agency, or rewriting large chunks of the code.

That’s why I don’t recommend vibe coding.

AI works best when you use it with a structured workflow and proper reviews using tools like @coderabbitai. That’s how you ship production-grade apps, not just hype demos.

Here’s the breakdown of the AI workflow we’ve refined after shipping 45+ SaaS projects. 👇🏻

tweets.text:
Every vibe-coded app looks the same

Here's how to fix yours so it stands out:

Step 1: Add micro-animations to page transitions 
Step 2: Add haptic feedback on every tap 
Step 3: Add subtle bounces to modals/sheets 
Step 4: Add motion to loading states

Tools: Claude Code (trained on Apple's animation library) 

Cost: $0 extra 

Time: 6 hours → app that "just feels different"

THE KEY: Details compound

Same app. Same code. 6 hours apart. 

One got 7 likes. One got 800 waitlist signups.

Users can't explain WHY your app feels premium. 

They just know it does.
